subtitle: Bhillama V and the Basalt Birth of Devagiri

panels.shot: epic wide of Bhillama V on horseback before a sheer black hill, dusk sky burning behind Devagiri’s rising ramparts
panels.action: Bhillama V sits straight on his horse, mail glinting, as workers and soldiers swarm over the dark basalt hill that will become Devagiri, scaffolds clinging to its sides under a copper-red evening sky.

dialogue.text: As the Chalukya throne in Kalyani trembles, Bhillama V turns a raw basalt hill into Devagiri – and rides toward Soratur, where empire will show him the cost of pushing beyond rock and fate.

i18n.hi: कल्याणी का चालुक्य सिंहासन डगमगाता है, भिल्लम पंचम कच्ची चट्टान से देवगिरि गढ़ता है – और सोरातूर की ओर बढ़ता है, जहाँ साम्राज्य उसे पत्थर और किस्मत से आगे बढ़ने की कीमत दिखाएगा।

panels.shot: somber bird’s-eye over Kalyani’s royal complex, half in shadow, half in fading light
panels.action: The aging palaces and temples of Kalyani sprawl under a hazy Deccan sky, courtyards quiet, banners drooping, as distant roads show petty armies marching without fear of the old capital.

dialogue.text: By the late twelfth century, Kalyani, proud seat of the Western Chalukyas, had grown tired. Its kings struggled, its feudatories grew bold, and the old order began to loosen, crack by crack.

i18n.hi: बारहवीं सदी के अंत तक पश्चिमी चालुक्यों की शान, कल्याणी थक चुकी थी। राजा कमजोर, सामंत हिम्मती, और पुराना सपना दरार दरार टूटने लगा था।

panels.shot: low-angle medium of Bhillama V in a council hall, half-lit, map of the western Deccan laid before him
panels.action: Bhillama V stands over a rough palm-leaf map spread on a stone table, finger resting near Sinnar and Devagiri, his face calm but intent as a few lesser chiefs watch him in wary silence.

dialogue.text: Among those feudatories were the Yadavas of Sinnar. Bhillama V saw what others feared to name: that a vassal could step out of the shadow, if he chose his ground carefully and moved before rivals did.

i18n.hi: इन सामंतों में सिन्नेऱ के यादव भी थे। भिल्लम पंचम ने वो देखा जिसे दूसरे कहने से डरते थे: कि जागीरदार भी छाया से बाहर कदम रख सकता है, अगर जमीन सही चुने और rivals से पहले चले।

panels.shot: sweeping wide of a column of horsemen leaving Sinnar’s countryside, dust rising
panels.action: Bhillama V rides at the head of a compact, disciplined cavalry band through the rocky scrub of the western Deccan, dust clouds trailing behind, watchtowers of minor chiefs shrinking in the distance.

dialogue.text: As Western Chalukya authority weakened, Bhillama began to act as more than a follower. His campaigns pushed outward, testing old borders and measuring how far Chalukya power truly reached now.

i18n.hi: जैसे–जैसे पश्चिमी चालुक्य सत्ता ढीली पड़ी, भिल्लम सिर्फ अनुयायी से आगे बढ़ा। उसकी चढ़ाइयाँ बाहर तक चलीं, पुराने सीमों को परखा और देखा कि चालुक्य ताकत अब कहाँ तक पहुँचती है।

panels.shot: dramatic wide of Bhillama V’s forces approaching Kalyani’s walls at dawn
panels.action: In the pale light of dawn, Bhillama V’s troops gather before the walls of Kalyani, siege engines being hauled forward, while the old city’s ramparts stand worn yet imposing against the sky.

dialogue.text: Around 1187, the contest reached Kalyani itself. With Chalukya strength drained, Bhillama moved on the capital, seizing what had once seemed unthinkable for a mere feudatory of the Deccan.

i18n.hi: लगभग 1187 में मुकाबला सीधे कल्याणी तक पहुँच गया। चालुक्य बल सूख चुका था, तो भिल्लम राजधानी पर चढ़ बैठा, वो छीनकर जो कभी दक्खिन के एक सामंत के लिए नामुमकिन लगता था।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Bhillama V entering Kalyani’s inner gateway, measured and composed
panels.action: Bhillama V rides through a heavy wooden gateway into Kalyani’s inner precinct, banners behind him, his face composed as curious townsfolk and wary nobles stand back, watching the change of power.

dialogue.text: Inscriptional clues and later accounts remember Bhillama as king at Kalyani. The old Chalukya stronghold did not vanish overnight, but its authority now answered to a different name.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख और बाद की कथाएँ भिल्लम को कल्याणी का राजा मानती हैं। पुराना चालुक्य गढ़ एक दिन में नहीं मिटा, पर उसकी सत्ता अब एक नए नाम को जवाब देती थी।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of the raw basalt hill of Devagiri under a harsh sun
panels.action: Under a white-hot Deccan sun, a dark, massive basalt hill rises from the plain, sides rough but steep, a few scrub trees clinging to ledges, with Bhillama V on horseback studying it from below.

dialogue.text: Yet Bhillama did not choose Kalyani as his lasting seat. His eye fell on a hard basalt hill near Sinnar, a block of stone thrust from the earth – Devagiri – whose shape promised defense and design.

i18n.hi: लेकिन भिल्लम ने कल्याणी को अपना स्थायी आसन नहीं चुना। उसकी नज़र सिन्नेऱ के पास के एक सख्त बेसाल्ट टीले पर गई – धरती से उठा पत्थर का टुकड़ा, देवगिरि – जिसका आकार खुद ही रक्षा और योजना का वादा करता था।

panels.shot: engineering-focused wide of early fort works on Devagiri, ramps, chisels, trenches
panels.action: Workers with chisels and hammers chip at the hill’s slopes, cutting them steeper, while others dig a deep trench that will become a moat; Bhillama V stands overseeing, gesturing toward gate locations.

dialogue.text: Devagiri’s rise was no miracle. Its slopes were carved sharper, a moat cut at its foot, paths laid in confusing angles, and gateways planned with heavy doors and iron spikes to cripple charging beasts.

i18n.hi: देवगिरि का उठना कोई चमत्कार नहीं था। ढालें और तेज काटी गईं, पाद में गहरी खाई खोदी, रास्ते उलझे मोड़ों से बिछाए गए, और फाटक भारी दरवाज़ों व लोहे की कीलों से भर दिए गए जो दौड़ते जानवरों को तोड़ दें।

panels.shot: medium shot near the gate, focusing on artisans fitting spikes and carpenters raising beams
panels.action: Carpenters raise solid timber beams into a gateframe while smiths fit long iron spikes onto a heavy door; Bhillama V inspects the work, hand resting on the rough wood, expression firm and approving.

dialogue.text: Design answered threat. A charging elephant would meet metal teeth, not splintering planks; attackers would be funneled along exposed approaches, where defenders could watch, wait, and strike from height.

i18n.hi: डिज़ाइन सीधे खतरे को जवाब देता था। चढ़ता हाथी लकड़ियाँ नहीं, लोहे के दाँतों से टकराता; दुश्मन खुले रास्तों से ही घुसते, जहाँ किले के रक्षक ऊपर से देख सकें, ठहर सकें और वार कर सकें।

panels.shot: interior cross-section style wide of zig-zagging approaches and hidden rock passages
panels.action: The hill’s inner slopes show narrow, angled paths winding upward, with a glimpse of a rock passage tunneled through the basalt; soldiers move along these ways, learning the turns that outsiders would not know.

dialogue.text: Later, rock passages would thread inside the hill, sheltering movement. False approaches misled the unfamiliar. Devagiri’s strength lay not in saying it was invincible, but in making attack costly.

i18n.hi: बाद में पत्थर के भीतर सुरंगें कटीं, जिसमें आवाजाही छुप सके। झूठे रास्ते अनजान को भटका देते। देवगिरि की ताकत उसके ‘अजय’ होने में नहीं, बल्कि हमला महँगा बनाने में थी।

panels.shot: majestic wide of Devagiri fort completed, banners of the Yadavas flying
panels.action: Devagiri now stands crowned with ramparts and towers on its summit, Yadava banners fluttering from its highest point; Bhillama V rides up the main ascent, soldiers lining the path in disciplined ranks.

dialogue.text: From this black hill rose a new capital. Devagiri became the heart of Bhillama’s Yadava realm, a stone answer to the uncertainty that had spread from Kalyani into the western Deccan.

i18n.hi: इस काली चट्टान से नया राजधानी उगा। देवगिरि भिल्लम के यादव राज्य का दिल बना, पत्थर का जवाब उस अनिश्चितता को जो कल्याणी से पश्चिमी दक्खिन तक फैल गई थी।

panels.shot: inscription-style close on a stone slab, with Bhillama faintly reflected reading it
panels.action: A stone inscription slab stands upright in a temple courtyard, its Kannada lines clear; Bhillama V’s figure is seen behind it, half-reflected on its polished surface as priests and scribes stand nearby.

dialogue.text: Bhillama’s Gadag and Mutugi inscriptions, dated 1189, speak of his raids and sovereignty. Through their carved words, we see a ruler who no longer called himself merely a Chalukya subordinate.

i18n.hi: भिल्लम के गदग और मुतुगी शिलालेख, 1189 के, उसकी चढ़ाइयों और सत्ता की बातें करते हैं। इन खुदे शब्दों में हम उस शासक को देखते हैं जो खुद को अब सिर्फ चालुक्य अधीन नहीं कहता।

panels.shot: strategic map-table medium, showing Gadag and Mutugi relative to Devagiri and Soratur
panels.action: Bhillama V stands over a more detailed map marked with Gadag, Mutugi, Devagiri and Soratur, small figurines set near each; his hand hovers over Soratur, brow slightly furrowed, as officers watch.

dialogue.text: These inscriptions fix him in the western Deccan, near centres like Gadag and Mutugi. But to hold a new kingdom, Bhillama had to measure himself not just against fading Chalukyas, but against rising neighbors.

i18n.hi: ये शिलालेख उसे पश्चिमी दक्खिन में, गदग और मुतुगी जैसे केन्द्रो के पास जमाते हैं। पर नया राज्य थामने के लिए भिल्लम को सिर्फ ढलते चालुक्यों से नहीं, उठते पड़ोसियों से भी भिड़कर खुद को तौलना था।

panels.shot: tense wide of Bhillama’s army marching toward Soratur, horizon dark with storm clouds
panels.action: Under a heavy sky, Bhillama V’s forces move toward the plains around Soratur, lines of cavalry and infantry stretching across the landscape, spears up, banners streaming ahead of an approaching storm front.

dialogue.speaker: bhillama_v
dialogue.text: If Devagiri is to stand as a kingdom, we must prove it in battle.

i18n.hi: अगर देवगिरि को राज्य बनकर टिकना है, तो मैदान में साबित करना होगा।

panels.shot: wide battle tableau at Soratur, Hoysala and Yadava hosts facing off, no gore
panels.action: Two disciplined armies confront each other near Soratur, lines bristling with spears and shields; war elephants stand between the ranks, drums upraised, as dust hangs in the air before the impending clash.

dialogue.text: Near Soratur, Bhillama met the Hoysalas. Ballala II’s Anekere inscription of 1192 remembers this battle; it tells of Yadava defeat, and of Jaitrapala, Bhillama’s son, falling in the fighting.

i18n.hi: सोरातूर के पास भिल्लम की भिड़न्त होयसलों से हुई। बल्लाल द्वितीय के 1192 के अनेकेरे शिलालेख इस युद्ध को याद रखते हैं; वे यादव पराजय और लड़ाई में भिल्लम के बेटे जैत्रपाल के गिरने की कथा सुनाते हैं।

panels.shot: dramatic medium of Bhillama V mid-battle, surrounded by confusion, looking toward a collapsing flank
panels.action: In the thick of dust and clashing arms, Bhillama V sits astride his horse, turning sharply toward a Yadava flank that is breaking, his jaw set as riders pull back and standard-bearers waver.

dialogue.text: The Hoysala record celebrates their triumph. It marks Jaitrapala’s death clearly, but is silent on Bhillama’s fate. Later tradition places the king’s end at Soratur, yet our inscriptions do not confirm that.

i18n.hi: होयसला लेख अपनी जीत का जश्न मनाता है। वो जैत्रपाल की मौत साफ दिखाता है, पर भिल्लम के अंत पर खामोश है। बाद की परम्परा राजा के अंत को सोरातूर पर रखती है, पर हमारे शिलालेख इसकी पुष्टि नहीं करते।

panels.shot: somber wide of the battlefield aftermath, weapons scattered, silhouettes of Hoysalas standing
panels.action: The battlefield lies quiet under a grey sky, abandoned spears and shields scattered across churned earth; in the distance, Hoysala soldiers stand grouped, while the Yadava banners lie trampled in the dust.

dialogue.text: Soratur taught Bhillama’s house a harsh lesson. Ambition had carried Yadava arms far from Devagiri’s rock, into ground where another power was ready, and where the price would be counted in sons and men.

i18n.hi: सोरातूर ने भिल्लम के घर को कड़ा सबक दिया। महत्त्वाकांक्षा यादव सेना को देवगिरि की चट्टान से दूर, ऐसी धरती पर ले गई जहाँ दूसरी ताकत तैयार थी, और कीमत बेटों और सिपाहियों में गिनी गई।

panels.shot: quiet medium of Bhillama V back at Devagiri, overlooking the plain from the ramparts at sunset
panels.action: Bhillama V stands alone on Devagiri’s high rampart at sunset, hands resting on the rough stone, gazing over the broad plain below where fields and roads stretch toward the dim horizon.

dialogue.text: What we can say with evidence is this: before and after Soratur, Devagiri remained. The hill-held capital was the frame within which later Yadavas would climb, falter, and face new storms from the north.

i18n.hi: जिस बात को सबूत से कह सकते हैं, वो ये है: सोरातूर से पहले और बाद भी देवगिरि टिका रहा। चट्टान पर टिकी राजधानी वही चौखट बनी, जिसमें बाद के यादव चढ़े, डगमगाए, और उत्तर से आने वाले नए तूफानों से भिड़े।

panels.shot: timeless bird’s-eye over Devagiri’s hill, crossfading hint to future sieges without showing them
panels.action: Devagiri’s basalt hill rises in serene light, its fortifications clear; faint ghost-like shadows of later armies appear at different points around it, suggesting future sieges, while the stone itself remains unchanged.

dialogue.text: Devagiri would surrender and fall more than once in later centuries. Bhillama’s work endures not as an unyielding miracle, but as a reminder that even the strongest fortress must know the limits of the kingdom behind it.

i18n.hi: आगे की सदियों में देवगिरि कई बार झुका और टूटा। भिल्लम की रचना किसी अटल चमत्कार के रूप में नहीं, बल्कि इस याद के रूप में बची कि सबसे मजबूत किला भी पीछे खड़े राज्य की हदें समझकर ही टिकता है।

title_i18n.en: The Hill That Would Not Yield
title_i18n.hi: वो पहाड़ी जो झुकने से इंकार करे
